page_title: Mastering Service Level Objective Implementation: A Practical Guide

summary.name: Succeeding with Service Level Objectives (IIDARR process)
summary.one_liner: A Squadcast blog guide by SRE Danny Mican on implementing Service Level Objectives (SLOs) step by step using the IIDARR process: Identify, Instrument, Define, Alert, Report/Refine.
use_cases: Rolling out SLOs across engineering teams
Choosing which operations to measure as SLIs
Setting initial SLO targets from historical data
Configuring burn rate alerts on error budgets
Deciding between reliability work and feature releases
summary.what_it_does: The article walks through the five-phase IIDARR framework for adopting SLOs: identifying key operations as SLIs, instrumenting them to produce queryable metrics, defining an SLO target (for example, using a 7, 14, or 30 day historical average), alerting on error budget burn, and reporting/refining through regular reviews. It gives concrete SLO examples for an eCommerce order processing time, cloud storage 99.9% availability, a CDN, and video buffering rate. It recommends two burn rate alerts per SLO (2% of budget in 1 hour, 10% in 1 day), drawn from Google's SRE Workbook. It also lists common anti-patterns such as relying on hope, SRE owning SLOs for teams, and static SLOs without feedback loops.
notable: Structured five-phase IIDARR framework for SLO adoption
Multiple burn rate alerting recommendation from Google's SRE Workbook
Guidance on using SLO history to balance reliability work against feature velocity
caveats: Page is a blog article, not a software tool; it mentions Squadcast's own on-call platform only in promotional lines
Refers to external resources (Google's Art of SLOs course, SRE Workbook) for in-depth detail
